item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 030520
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Fri Oct 2 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Nolo, located several hundred miles west of the main Hawaiian
Islands, and on Hurricane Rachel, located just over a couple of
hundred miles south-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form late this weekend or
early next week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is likely to form by the middle of next
week while the system moves slowly west-northwestward to
northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Fri Oct 02 2026 
180 
WTPZ33 KNHC 030239
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM MST Fri Oct 02 2026
 
...RACHEL CONTINUES WESTWARD AS IT PASSES SOCORRO ISLAND...
...SOME WEAKENING EXPECTED OVER NEXT SEVERAL DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.4N 111.5W
ABOUT 265 MI...425 KM SSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...966 MB...28.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 19.4 North, longitude 111.5 West. Rachel is moving
toward the west near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this general motion is
expected to continue tonight. A gradual turn toward the 
west-northwest with an increase in forward speed is expected on 
Saturday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts. Some weakening is expected over the next day or two. However,
Rachel is expected to remain a hurricane for the next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 966 mb (28.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect the coast of
west-central Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula through the
weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Beven

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Fri Oct 02 2026 
014 
WTPZ43 KNHC 030240
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM MST Fri Oct 02 2026

The convective structure of Rachel has remained largely unchanged 
since the previous advisory. Visible satellite imagery continues to 
show a cloud-filled eye inside a central dense overcast (CDO), with 
much of the deeper convection displaced slightly to the west of the 
center due to moderate northeasterly wind shear. The latest 
subjective intensity estimate from TAFB is T4.5/77 kt, while 
objective estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 79 to 94 kt. The 
initial intensity is lowered slightly to 85 kt for this advisory, 
blending the subjective and objective estimates.

The initial motion is estimated to be 280/4 kt, or slowly westward. 
This slow westward motion is expected to continue, with a gradual 
increase in forward speed and a turn toward the west-northwest over 
the weekend as the ridge begins to weaken. While the track guidance 
is in fair agreement with this scenario, there is some guidance 
disagreement regarding the timing of the forward speed early next 
week. The updated track forecast closely aligns with the previous 
advisory through 96 h, then nudges slightly southward thereafter, 
lying near the reliable HCCA consensus model.
 
Rachel is forecast to encounter moderate northeasterly vertical wind 
shear and a moisture-starved environment, which should initiate a 
weakening trend over the next several days. Sea-surface temperatures 
(SSTs) along the hurricane's path will decrease from 29 to 27C over 
the next 36 to 48 h as Rachel moves through the cold wake of 
Hurricane Polo, further expediting this weakening. Beyond that time, 
SSTs should rebound slightly to 28C as the cyclone exits the cold 
wake, though it will be entering an increasingly dry mid-level 
environment. These competing factors are expected to result in 
little net change in strength during the 48- to 72-hour period, and 
the NHC intensity forecast continues to flatline Rachel at 70 kt. By 
96 to 120 hours, Rachel is forecast to cross sub-26C waters and 
encounter even drier air, inducing steady weakening back to tropical 
storm strength by the end of the forecast period.
